topic.para: The purpose of RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks) is to combine multiple physical block devices or partitions into a single logical virtual volume to optimize I/O performance, data redundancy, or both. Enterprise hardware RAID controllers typically use SAS, SCSI, or NVMe protocols because they handle deep command queues and parallel I/O processing efficiently, though SATA controllers are also supported. Linux software RAID (MD-RAID) provides the full feature set of enterprise RAID systems without the added cost or single point of failure of proprietary hardware controllers. While parity calculations require minor CPU and memory resources, modern multi-core processors with SIMD instruction sets easily handle software RAID workloads—even on high-throughput NVMe storage arrays.
